## Primary sources checked

- Evans--Smart, “Everywhere differentiability of infinity harmonic functions,” 2011, DOI `10.1007/s00526-010-0388-1`: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00526-010-0388-1. The article states that every infinity-harmonic function is differentiable, and its introduction says continuous differentiability in dimensions `n>=3` remained open at the time.
- Evans--Savin, “C^{1,alpha} regularity for infinity harmonic functions in two dimensions,” 2008, DOI `10.1007/s00526-007-0143-4`: https://www.math.columbia.edu/~savin/evans-savin.pdf. Their method establishes a positive planar exponent, with the higher-dimensional proof conditional on further estimates.
- Kai Xu, “Infinity-harmonic functions and inverse mean curvature flow clusters,” arXiv:2607.06698 (July 2026): https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06698. The primary abstract claims planar `C^{1,1/3}` and additional structure, so the 2D endpoint is no longer the target here.

Updated 2026-10-09. Status: exploratory proof work; no endpoint theorem established.

## Source pins and verification status

- Astra start interface: `harjassand/astra-research-knowledge`, commit `031ce532f7f6d1c070387f6213a00204893be79d`; `00_START_HERE.txt` was fetched at this exact ref and routes task-first retrieval.

The source tree is `preprints/Uniform-Interior-C1alpha-Estimates-for-Infinity-Harmonic-Functions-October-4-2026/build/manuscript/`.
- Family 377 is a 46-page Oct. 4, 2026 manuscript. The repository's `lean/docs/377.md` is citation/scope metadata, not a proof formalization. The family page says no Lean formalization and no expert review is recorded. OpenAI's README itself says released results are at different verification stages and unformalized results may have issues.
- The source proof sections inspected: `01-introduction.tex`, `02-flatness.tex`, `03-reduction.tex`, `04-limiting-tools.tex`, `05-envelope-contact.tex`, `06-discrete-propagation.tex`, `07-contact-localization.tex`, `08-rigidity.tex`.

## Exact next theorem

For each integer `d >= 3`, does there exist `C_d` such that every viscosity infinity-harmonic `u` on `B_1 subset R^d` satisfies

`||Du||_{L-infinity(B_{1/2})} + [Du]_{C^{0,1/3}(B_{1/2})} <= C_d osc_{B_1} u`?

The exponent is optimal: Aronsson's example `u=(|x_1|^{4/3}-|x_2|^{4/3})/2`, extended independently of the other coordinates, has `|Du(te_1)-Du(0)|=(2/3)|t|^{1/3}`. Any exponent above `1/3` fails.

Family 377 claims uniform `C^{1,alpha_d}` for `d>=3`, with `alpha_d` positive but non-explicit. It explicitly makes no endpoint claim. The radial Coulomb construction now has a complete computer-assisted existence argument within its exact stated scope. The interval certificate, analytic construction, and adversarial code review are included. This is not proof-assistant certification, external specialist review, or established historical priority.

MAIN RESULT
There exists a smooth compactly supported rotationally symmetric probability density on R^2, supported on five disjoint annuli, for which the identical-three-marginal Coulomb optimal-transport problem has a finite attained Kantorovich minimum but no optimal Borel Monge pair. This rules out every graph optimizer, including nonsymmetric ones, rather than only selected Seidl maps. The Monge infimum still equals the Kantorovich minimum; nonattainment is the conclusion.
